title: The Philip K. Dick Reader
author: Philip K. Dick
card_summary: A major short story collection spanning Dick's career, at 505 pages. Described on the back cover with a Wall Street Journal quote praising Dick's ability to put readers inside people's minds. The Philip K. Dick Reader demonstrates the range that has led many readers to consider him the greatest science fiction mind on any planet. Published posthumously as interest in Dick's work continued to mount.
page_summary:
The Philip K. Dick Reader is a comprehensive short story collection published posthumously, running to 505 pages. The back cover features a quote from The Wall Street Journal praising Dick's distinctive ability to immerse readers in his characters' consciousness.

The collection was published during a period of rapidly growing interest in Dick's work following his death in 1982. As the back cover notes, Dick's reputation has been enhanced by a growing body of critical attention, and The Philip K. Dick Award is now given annually to a distinguished work of science fiction. The volume represents an effort to make Dick's extensive short fiction catalog accessible to the expanding audience discovering his work through film adaptations and critical reassessment.

At over 500 pages, The Philip K. Dick Reader is one of the most substantial single-volume collections of Dick's short fiction, providing readers with a broad survey of his work in the form. Dick wrote over 120 short stories during his career, and this collection draws from that vast output to present a representative selection of his most important and entertaining short fiction.

**==> picture [500 x 32] intentionally omitted <==**

Many thousands of readers consider Philip K. Dick the greatest science fiction mind on _any_ planet.  Since his untimely death in 1982, interest in Dick's works has continued to mount, and his reputation has been further enhanced by a growing body of critical attention.  The Philip K. Dick Award is now given annually to a distinguished work of science fiction, and the Philip K. Dick Society is devoted to the study and promulgation of his works. 

Dick won the prestigious Hugo Award for the best novel of 1963 for _The Man in the High Castle_ .  In the last year of his life, the exciting film _Blade Runner_ was made from his novel _Do Androids Dream of Electric Sheep?_ 

This collection includes some of Dick's earliest short and medium-length fiction, including "We Can Remember It for You Wholesale" (the story that inspired _Total Recall_ ), "Second Variety" (which inspired _Screamers_ ), "Paycheck", "The Minority Report", and twenty more.
